target_customer: Operations teams at small and mid sized companies
problem: Ops teams run manual workflows that need both automation and human judgment, and building internal tools needed engineers.
product_category: No code workflow and internal tools

founders.name: Omar Skalli
founders.background_notes: Later Head of Growth Engineering at Notion, per YC page.

exit.reason: Team acquired by Notion; the product shut down on 2022-09-30 per the company's own notice.

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual workflow builder with human in the loop steps and integrations, standard but broad for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Workflows built by customers create lock in, but no-code and automation tools were crowded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Notion hired the team in 2022 and the product was shut down on 2022-09-30.

market_need_then: No code tooling was growing in 2020 and ops teams lacked engineering help; specific spend data was not found.

identity.logo: Simple wordmark logo on a minimal page
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, personal and mission focused; mission to let everyone build software

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press found; the compound name resembles many other flow tools.

outcome_analysis: Flowdash built a no code workflow tool for ops teams and raised a small reported amount, around 300 thousand dollars per CB Insights, before Notion acquired the team and shut the product down on 30 September 2022. The shutdown notice and the deal framing suggest a team acquisition without continuing the product, though the terms are undisclosed.
notes: Funding figures (about 300K over three rounds, latest 150K seed April 2020, investors Liquid 2, Gradient Ventures, Y Combinator, Soma Capital) come only from CB Insights, unverified, so no rounds are recorded. Acquisition date inferred from the company notice about the 2022-09-30 shutdown. Competitor search returned only 2023 to 2026 content, so the list is empty.
